nodes.title: [Bug]: chrome.webRequest is schema-registered but has no bindings in MV3 service workers, crashing worker registration
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

An MV3 extension with the `webRequest` permission can register observational listeners (e.g. `chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(...)`) in its background service worker, as it can in Chrome.

### Actual Behavior

The `webRequest` API feature/schema is registered — `typeof chrome.webRequest === 'object'` inside the worker — but the renderer bindings module resources are missing from the resource bundle:

```
ERROR:extensions/renderer/resource_bundle_source_map.cc:72] NOTREACHED hit. Module resource registered as "webRequest" not found
ERROR:extensions/renderer/resource_bundle_source_map.cc:72] NOTREACHED hit. Module resource registered as "webRequestEvent" not found
"(BLESSED_EXTENSION context for <id>) No source for require(webRequest)"
```

As a result `chrome.webRequest` is an empty object, `chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` is `undefined`, the worker throws at top level, and MV3 service worker registration fails entirely:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addListener')
Service worker registration failed. Status code: 15
```

Because the registration failure takes the whole worker down, any real-world extension whose worker touches `chrome.webRequest` at startup is completely non-functional (observed with NordPass, whose action button is driven by its worker). This half-registered state is arguably worse than the API being absent — extensions that feature-detect `chrome.webRequest` pass the check and then crash.

Full log: see the gist.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/dep/ec59df61562cfb3af21031a660e733b4

### Additional Information

- Follow-up to the MV3 support push in #37876 (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/37876#issuecomment-1656808686) — service worker registration, `chrome.scripting`, and `chrome.tabs` all work great now; `chrome.webRequest` appears to be the next-most-impactful gap for MV3 extensions.
- `chrome.declarativeNetRequest` is entirely `undefined` in the same context (expected, since it is not on the supported-API list, but noting it since MV3 network-observing extensions typically need one of the two).
- Prior art: #2115 (2016 request for `chrome.webRequest.*`, closed), #19447 (//extensions integration tracking issue, closed).
- Two plausible resolutions from the outside: (a) pack the `webRequest`/`webRequestEvent` custom-bindings resources and wire the browser-side `WebRequestAPI`/event router so the API actually works, or (b) stop registering the schema so the API is cleanly absent and feature-detection in extensions behaves. (a) is obviously the dream. 🙏

Update after digging into the Electron source and testing against nightly: root cause found, and the picture splits into two distinct problems:

## 1. The crash is a packaging regression in Electron 43, already fixed on `main` — needs backport

Between Chromium 149 → 150 (Electron 42 → 43), the extensions renderer bindings JS moved out of `extensions_renderer_resources.grd` into a new grit target, `extensions_renderer_generated_resources.pak` (`extensions/renderer/resources/BUILD.gn`). Electron 43's `build/electron_paks.gni` still repacks only `extensions_renderer_resources.pak` + `extensions_resources.pak`, so the generated pak is built but never included in `resources.pak` → `NOTREACHED` in `resource_bundle_source_map.cc:72` → `chrome.webRequest` has no members.

- This is **not MV3-specific**: an MV2 persistent background page fails identically on 43.0.0 (same `NOTREACHED` pair, `onBeforeRequest` undefined). The `spec/fixtures/extensions/chrome-webRequest` tests can't pass on the shipped 43 build.
- `main` already contains the fix, incidentally, via #51804 (the resource-allowlist work packs `extensions_renderer_generated_resources.pak`). Verified on `electron-nightly` 45.0.0-nightly.20260703: bindings load, no crash, worker registration succeeds, and **MV2 background-page `onBeforeRequest` events fire correctly**.
- Neither `43-x-y` nor `44-x-y` has the fix. Since this is a regression that silently broke all extension `chrome.webRequest` usage (and crashes every MV3 worker that touches it), a backport of that one pak line to both branches would be 🙏.

## 2. After the fix, MV3 service workers still receive no webRequest events (repro's second act)

On the same nightly (45.0.0-nightly.20260703), with bindings loading fine:

- MV3 worker registers `chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(..., {urls: ['<all_urls>']})` without error (manifest has `webRequest` permission + `<all_urls>` in `host_permissions`; also tried it in `permissions`).
- Loading `https://example.com` in a `BrowserWindow` on the same session fires **zero events** in the worker, while the identical listener in an MV2 background page fires as expected.

So the browser→service-worker webRequest event dispatch path (lazy/SW listeners in the WebRequest event router) appears unwired independently of the packaging issue. Happy to file this as a separate issue if that's cleaner — the net effect for MV3 extensions like password managers is the same "worker can't observe requests" gap this issue describes.

(Side note from the same investigation, in case it's useful triage context: `chrome.declarativeNetRequest` dynamic rules **do** enforce correctly on stock 43.0.0 when the permission is declared — my original repro saw `undefined` only because the manifest lacked the `declarativeNetRequest` permission. Static `rule_resources` never load, though — `getEnabledRulesets()` returns `[]` — presumably because install-time ruleset indexing never runs. And registering any `session.webRequest` listener disables both extension webRequest *and* dNR enforcement for those loader factories, per the precedence rule in `docs/api/extensions.md`.)

@Dhananjay0117
https://www.instagram.com/roshni_modanval97080?igsh=MWkyeWYzMHo2bG5tcQ==
https://www.instagram.com/roshni_modanval97080?igsh=MWkyeWYzMHo2bG5tcQ==
https://www.instagram.com/roshni_modanval97080?igsh=MWkyeWYzMHo2bG5tcQ==
@dep to be clear, are you saying https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51804 fixes this issue for you?
@dep any update?

Requesting a backport to 43-x-y

As @dep diagnosed, this is a packaging regression in Electron 43: the extensions renderer bindings moved into extensions_renderer_generated_resources.pak in Chromium 150, but build/electron_paks.gni on 43-x-y was never updated to repack it, so the bindings JS is missing at runtime.

The fix is already merged on main via [#51804](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51804) (Linux) and [#52290](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52290) (macOS) — shipping in Electron 44 — but both are labeled no-backport.

Could maintainers consider targeting these to 43-x-y? It's a regression that breaks any MV3 extension using chrome.webRequest entirely (service worker registration fails at startup), with no workaround from the extension side. The change is build/packaging config only, so backport risk should be low.

Happy to test a backport build. Thanks!

nodes.title: Allow monospaced digit fonts for menu item labels on macOS
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description On macOS, menu item labels are rendered with the system menu font, whose digits are proportional. So any menu showing a column of numbers comes out jagged, because e.g. `11:15` renders narrower than `09:45`: There's currently no way around this: `MenuItem.label` maps to `NSMenuItem.title`, and Electron exposes neither `attributedTitle` nor any font option. In a native app this is a one-liner: set `attributedTitle` with `monospacedDigitSystemFontOfSize:`, the SF variant with tabular figures that's otherwise identical to the menu font. #22363 solved the same problem for the tray title with `tray.setTitle(title, { fontType: 'monospacedDigit' })`. Menu item labels never got the equivalent, so a tray calendar can align its countdown but not the time column in its dropdown. ### Proposed Solution The same `fontType` option on `MenuItem`, macOS-only like `toolTip`: ```js new MenuItem({ label: "11:15 Doctor's appointment", fontType: 'monospacedDigit' }) ``` The implementation looks small: when the option is set, `electron_menu_controller.mm` renders the label via `attributedTitle` with the corresponding font variant, analogous to the `fontType` handling in `tray_icon_cocoa.mm`. Supporting both tray values (`monospaced` and `monospacedDigit`) keeps the two APIs symmetric. ### Alternatives Considered - Padding with figure spaces (U+2007): Still unequal widths, the digits themselves are proportional - Unicode fullwidth/monospace digits: Wrong font, looks out of place - Pre-rendering the time column into template `NativeImage` icons: What we ship today – works well, but adds a lot of machinery for one line of AppKit ### Additional Information I attached [menu-item-font-type.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29671470/menu-item-font-type.patch) mirroring the `toolTip` per-item plumbing and the tray `fontType` implementation. It was drafted with Claude Fable 5, and I'm currently unable to build Electron locally – so it's untested. Happy to open a PR from it so CI can validate it, or for a maintainer to adopt or rework it instead.

Thanks for reporting!

> It was drafted with Claude Fable 5, and I'm currently unable to build Electron locally – so it's untested. Happy to open a PR from it so CI can validate it, or for a maintainer to adopt or rework it instead.

Attaching the patch was the right move. Thanks! Please don't open untested PRs. (We get too many of them already due to AI.)
I can take this one over the line, I think it's a good idea given that we already support it on tray: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52269

nodes.title: [Bug]: macOS: every keystroke in any input/textarea recreates a native autofill popup NSWindow, blocking the browser process 100-260 ms per key on macOS 26 (worst with CJK IME)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3 (the relevant code is unchanged on `main`)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — the popup churn exists in all recent versions; it became user-visible on macOS 26, where window ordering waits on synchronous WindowServer transactions.

### Expected Behavior

Typing into an `<input>` or `<textarea>` that has no datalist suggestions should not create or destroy native windows, and should not block the browser process.

### Actual Behavior

Every keystroke that changes the value of a focused `<input>`/`<textarea>` (with the caret at the end) makes the renderer send `ElectronAutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` **with an empty suggestion list**, and the browser process destroys and recreates a native autofill popup `NSWindow` each time. On macOS 26, each of those window-ordering operations blocks `CrBrowserMain` for 50–350 ms in a synchronous WindowServer transaction. Since `CrBrowserMain` routes all input events, **every window and input of the app stutters**.

CJK IME users are hit hardest: apps that type into a hidden textarea (e.g. xterm.js terminals) never change the textarea value for plain keys (keydown is `preventDefault()`ed), but **IME preedit lives in the textarea and changes its value on every keystroke** — so composition triggers the churn on every key. This was discovered while investigating Japanese-IME typing jank in [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) (an Electron-based terminal/agent app), where the jank affects the whole UI while composing.

Root cause chain (all verified):

1. **Renderer** — `AutofillAgent::ShowSuggestions` (`shell/renderer/electron_autofill_agent.cc`) reaches `ShowPopup(element, {}, {})` for any editable with a non-empty value and caret at end, **even when there are zero datalist suggestions** — including `<textarea>`, which can never have any. `TextFieldValueChanged` fires per keystroke (and per `compositionupdate` during IME composition).
2. **Browser** — `AutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` (`shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver.cc`) calls `AutofillPopup::CreateView` (`shell/browser/ui/autofill_popup.cc`), which unconditionally `Hide()`s the previous popup and creates + shows a new native child window — even for an empty list. Net effect: one NSWindow destroy + create + order-in per keystroke.
3. **macOS 26** — `sample(1)` of the browser process during typing shows `CrBrowserMain` blocked in:

   ```text
   -[NSWindow _doOrderWindow:]
     -[NSCGSWindow(NSCGSWindowOrdering) isOrderedIn]
       SLSWindowIsOrderedIn (SkyLight)
         SLSConnectionSynchronizeSLSCATransaction
           _SLSTransactionWaitSource → mach_msg2_trap   ← 1961 of 2006 samples
   ```

Evidence from a real 90 s Japanese-typing session in Orca (`devtools.timeline` + `toplevel` + `latencyInfo` trace): 74 `Receive mojo message` tasks ≥ 30 ms tagged `electron.mojom.ElectronAutofillDriver` on `CrBrowserMain`, totalling **10.1 s** with a **263 ms** max; 15 of 23 keydowns with > 100 ms `InputLatency::RawKeyDown` overlapped one of those tasks. Renderer-side handlers took 1–2 ms — the latency is entirely browser-process dispatch delay.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/hirorocky/82b35c2604e29b80883921b806a711ac

### Additional Information

The testcase needs no IME: it synthesizes composition updates via `webContents.debugger` (`Input.imeSetComposition`) into a plain autofocused `<textarea>`, and measures browser-process main-thread stalls with a 16 ms timer-drift monitor (the Node event loop shares `CrBrowserMain`, so synchronous WindowServer waits appear as timer drift).

Results on macOS 26.4.1 / Electron 42.3.3 / M-series:

```text
# textarea focused (autofill popup churn):
50 synthetic IME composition updates in 6957 ms
main-process event-loop stalls >50ms: count=37 total=4915 ms max=350 ms

# CONTROL=1 (textarea blurred, no editable target → no autofill traffic):
50 synthetic IME composition updates in 5220 ms
main-process event-loop stalls >50ms: count=1 total=118 ms max=118 ms
```

Manual repro: run the same app and type into the textarea with a Japanese/Chinese/Korean IME — the Event Timing API logs keydown durations in the hundreds of ms.

The same measurement against **VS Code 1.125.1 (Electron 42.2.0)** on the same machine reproduces identically — VS Code ships the same code and is not immune: 25 synthetic composition updates into its integrated terminal (a real xterm.js helper textarea) produced 26 `ElectronAutofillDriver` tasks totalling **1081 ms (max 163 ms)** on CrBrowserMain; a plain `<input>` in its workbench produced 333 ms. VS Code's *editor* escapes only because Monaco keeps the caret mid-value in its hidden textarea, which fails the `requires_caret_at_end` check.

Causality was also confirmed in-app with the caret condition alone: keeping a zero-width sentinel after the caret during composition (so `SelectionEnd() != value.length()`) drops the same 25-keystroke workload from **1208 ms to 0 ms** of browser-main blocking — the messages still flow, but the cheap `HideAutofillPopup` path replaces the popup-window rebuild.

Why editors like VS Code (Monaco) escape this: Monaco keeps surrounding context in its hidden textarea with the caret mid-value, so the `requires_caret_at_end` check in `ShowSuggestions` fails and only the cheap `HidePopup` path runs. xterm.js keeps the caret at the end of the preedit, hitting the expensive path on every composition update.

**Proposed fix** — mirror Chromium and only show the popup when there are suggestions:

```cc
// shell/renderer/electron_autofill_agent.cc, AutofillAgent::ShowSuggestions
  std::vector<std::u16string> data_list_values;
  std::vector<std::u16string> data_list_labels;
  if (!input_element.IsNull()) {
    GetDataListSuggestions(input_element, &data_list_values, &data_list_labels);
  }
  if (data_list_values.empty()) {
    HidePopup();
    return;
  }
  ShowPopup(element, data_list_values, data_list_labels);
```

`AutofillPopup::Hide()` is already a no-op when nothing is showing, so the steady-state cost for suggestion-less fields becomes zero. A belt-and-suspenders guard in `AutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` (`if (values.empty()) { autofill_popup_->Hide(); return; }`) would additionally protect against compromised renderers.

This is likely a meaningful contributor to the broader "Electron apps feel sluggish on macOS 26" class of reports (e.g. #48311 discusses SLS transaction sensitivity): the per-keystroke popup churn predates Tahoe but used to be cheap; Tahoe's synchronous WindowServer transactions turned it into user-visible input latency. Full `sample(1)` output and the 90 s trace are retained and can be shared on request.

Corroborating evidence from the archives: #26667 (2020) is a debug-build DCHECK crash — `Check failed: !clamped_content_size.IsEmpty(). Zero-sized windows not supported on Mac` — with exactly this call stack (`ElectronAutofillDriverStubDispatch::Accept` → `AutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` → `AutofillPopup::CreateView` → `AutofillPopupView::Show` → `SetBounds`), observed while running Slack. That is the empty-suggestion popup described here being created with zero size: debug builds have been asserting on this exact misbehavior since at least 2020, release builds just silently paid for the window churn — until macOS 26 made each one cost 100+ ms. The proposed fix (skip `ShowPopup` when there are no datalist suggestions) would also resolve that six-year-old DCHECK.

Thanks for reporting!

Does this window recreation also happen in Chrome?

No — I ran the identical workload against Chrome on the same machine (Chrome 149.0.7827.199, macOS 26.4.1, arm64), driving 50 synthetic composition updates via CDP (`Input.imeSetComposition`, 120 ms apart) into the same test page:

```text
# Chrome, <textarea> focused:
autofill-tagged mojo messages on CrBrowserMain: count=106 total=5 ms  max=0 ms
browser-main long tasks (>=30 ms):              count=0   total=0 ms

# Chrome, <input> focused:
autofill-tagged mojo messages on CrBrowserMain: count=159 total=15 ms max=3 ms
browser-main long tasks (>=30 ms):              count=0   total=0 ms

# Electron 42.3.3/43.0.0 fiddle, same workload (from the report above):
main-process event-loop stalls >50 ms:          count=37  total=4915 ms max=350 ms
```

The Event Timing API in the page shows every composition event completing in 16–24 ms with 0 ms input delay — Chrome stays perfectly smooth on the same macOS build.

The reason is architectural: Chromium's renderer-side agent *queries* the browser (`AskForValuesToFill`) instead of pushing a show command, and the browser only creates/shows the popup when it actually has suggestions. With zero suggestions it explicitly hides instead — `AutofillExternalDelegate::OnSuggestionsReturned` in `components/autofill/core/browser/ui/autofill_external_delegate.cc`:

```cc
if (suggestions.empty() && !IsAtMemoryTriggerSource(trigger_source)) {
    ...
    // No suggestions, any popup currently showing is obsolete.
    manager_->client().HideSuggestions(SuggestionHidingReason::kNoSuggestions, ...);
```

So the autofill IPC traffic per keystroke exists in Chrome too (as the message counts above show), but it never turns into native window creation/destruction. Electron's `AutofillAgent::ShowSuggestions` is the divergence: it reaches `ShowPopup(element, {}, {})` with an empty datalist, and `AutofillPopup::CreateView` then rebuilds the native window unconditionally. That is what the proposed fix aligns with Chromium's behavior.

nodes.title: Windows 11 (build 26200) + AMD RX 9070: Chromium GPU process fails during startup (`GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Electron 39.8.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should launch normally.


Maybe duplicate of : https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/52098
https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51761

Affected applications:

* Obsidian 1.12.7
* Signal Desktop 8.17.0
* Discord (latest)

Not affected:

* Visual Studio Code 1.126.0

## Environment

* OS: Windows 11 Pro
* Build: 26200.8737
* GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070
* Driver: 32.0.31021.5001
* Secondary GPU: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics






### Actual Behavior

## Actual Behavior

Multiple Electron applications terminate during startup.

The logs consistently end with:

```text
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415]
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

Signal additionally reports repeated GPU process failures before aborting:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
```

Windows Event Viewer records Application Error (Event ID 1000) with exception code:

```
0x80000003
```

The faulting module is the application executable itself (e.g. `Obsidian.exe`, `Signal.exe`).

## Reproduction

Launching Obsidian normally:

```powershell
& "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Obsidian\Obsidian.exe"
```

Results in:

* application exits almost immediately
* log ends with `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`

The same behavior is observed with Signal Desktop and Discord.

## Startup Flag Testing

### `--in-process-gpu`

Launching with:

```text
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior:

* the process no longer exits immediately
* however, the application window is not rendered correctly (GUI is missing / blank)

### Four-flag combination

Launching with:

```text
--disable-gpu
--disable-gpu-compositing
--disable-software-rasterizer
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior further.

In Safe Mode, this combination allows the UI to render instead of immediately terminating.

Outside Safe Mode, startup behavior changes, but rendering is still incomplete or absent.

The fact that `--in-process-gpu` consistently changes the failure mode suggests the issue is related to Chromium's GPU process initialization.

## Diagnostics Already Performed

* Updated AMD driver to latest available version
* `sfc /scannow`
* Windows Defender scan
* Malwarebytes scan
* HDR disabled
* Safe Mode testing
* AMD Radeon Software terminated
* DxDiag reports no display or DirectX problems

None of the above resolved the issue.

If there are additional Chromium or Electron logging flags that would help diagnose why the GPU process exits, I would be happy to collect and provide them.

### Testcase Gist URL

`npx electron`

### Additional Information

Visual Studio Code launches normally on the same machine.

This suggests the issue is not a complete Electron failure, but may depend on the Electron/Chromium version or GPU initialization path used by different applications.

<!-- end-of-life -->

Hello @NeytirX. Thanks for reporting this and helping to make Electron better!

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://www.electronjs.org/releases/stable) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.

> npx electron

yes, same issue

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10.0.19045 (6466)

### What arch are you using?

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Calling `Menu.setApplicationMenu()` while the user interacts with an open menu should not crash the app.

### Actual Behavior

If the application menu is replaced while being displayed, and a GC triggers before the menu closes, the relevant `Menu` object will be garbage-collected, causing various kinds of segfaults in menu-related UI code.

For example:
```

10  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
11  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
12  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
13  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
14  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
15  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
16  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)

19  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
20  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
21  Figma.exe                       0x7ff622ce48fe      views::View::PaintFromPaintRoot (view.cc:3122)
22  Figma.exe                       0x7ff622d60191      ui::Layer::PaintContentsToDisplayList (layer.cc:1599)
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-figma/103e9c2d491975cbefe183bfa5ca3cc5

### Additional Information

To trigger the issue in Fiddle, you need to run the app with `--js-flags=--expose-gc`, open the File menu, and mouse over the menu a bit.

This issue was introduced in 41.2.1, almost definitely in #50915 (the backport of #50465).

That PR contains a bunch of GC-related changes, one of which was the removal of a `gin_helper::SelfKeepAlive` property from `Menu`. I think [the premise of the change was that this was redundant](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50806#pullrequestreview-4079112260), since `Menu` instances are all owned by other objects that should retain them properly.

The problem with this is that the owner of a `Menu` will only retain it as long as it hasn't been replaced. If you replace the menu while it's open, and the `Menu` object gets garbage-collected as a result, its destructor will clear all of the delegate pointers that are still being used by the rendered views.

I tried just restoring the `SelfKeepAlive` and it did fix the issue for me, although I'm not sure if there's some reason that we would need to do this differently now. I'll put up a PR in a second.

nodes.title: [Bug]: globalShortcut portal path collapses F-key and punctuation accelerators to the same command id
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (any version with the Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal path)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Any Linux Wayland session using the org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts path

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Expected Behavior

Registering two shortcuts like `Ctrl+F9` and `Ctrl+F10` on the Wayland portal path binds two distinct portal shortcuts.

### Actual Behavior

`GlobalShortcut::Register` builds the portal command id from `extensions::Command::AcceleratorToString(accelerator)`, which only supports A–Z, 0–9, comma, period, arrows, Home/End/PgUp/PgDn, Space, Tab, Insert/Delete, and the media keys — everything else (all F-keys, Escape, Enter, most punctuation, numpad) returns an empty string. All such accelerators therefore collapse to the same empty command id and the same fake extension id, colliding in `command_callback_map_` and in the portal session: only the last registered shortcut of that class is actually bound, and its activation runs the last-registered callback.

Observed empirically: registering `Control+Shift+F9` produces a portal command whose id is derived from an empty accelerator string.

### Additional Information

Two possible directions: extend the stringification used for portal command ids to cover all registrable accelerators (needs to stay stable across versions, since the portal persists binds keyed by these ids), or key commands by something independent of the accelerator (with a migration for existing persisted binds). Related plumbing work: #52218.

Do you think it makes sense to fix this [upstream](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:ui/base/accelerators/command.cc;l=109;drc=44a8870df7a35fbb96ac69e14108317b95259ce4)? Do you think Chrome would want to support those keys, too?

One more collapse case this doesn't list yet: `AcceleratorToString` also returns `""` when `HasValidModifierCombination` fails ([command.cc L110](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/150.0.7871.250:ui/base/accelerators/command.cc;l=110)), so accelerators with no modifier, or with Shift as the only modifier, collapse into the same id as well.

Tested on Electron 43.5.0 (Hyprland 0.56.2, xdg-desktop-portal 1.22.1, `--enable-features=GlobalShortcutsPortal`): registering `Control+Shift+X`, `Control+Alt+A`, `Control+F10`, `Shift+A` and `A` returns `true` for all five, but `BindShortcuts` carries only three shortcuts. `Control+F10`, `Shift+A` and `A` end up as one `<prefix>-` entry with `preferred_trigger` `"a"`, and triggering it runs the callback for `A` (the last one registered). The command-id code is unchanged on `main`.

On @nikwen's question: I don't think this is Chromium's to fix. `AcceleratorToString` is the inverse of `Command::ParseImpl` (the keys at L275-285 match the switch at L141-205), i.e. the extension `commands` grammar ([documented rules](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/commands)), and Chrome never uses it for portal ids: the Linux listener builds ids from `command.command_name()` ([L181](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/150.0.7871.250:ui/base/accelerators/global_accelerator_listener/global_accelerator_listener_linux.cc;l=181), [L195](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/150.0.7871.250:ui/base/accelerators/global_accelerator_listener/global_accelerator_listener_linux.cc;l=195)), and the only Chrome caller of `OnCommandsChanged` passes the extension's named commands ([extension_commands_global_registry.cc L181](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/150.0.7871.250:chrome/browser/extensions/extension_commands_global_registry.cc;l=181)), even ones with no accelerator.

The collapse comes from Electron using `AcceleratorToString` as the command name. Keeping that name whenever it is non-empty and only falling back to an Electron-side string for `""` would fix it without changing ids for existing persisted binds.

nodes.title: A configurable build system using a file like electron.config.js
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While working on several Electron projects, I noticed that many desktop applications don't actually use a large portion of the Chromium features that are included by default.

Applications such as launchers, utilities, configuration tools, local dashboards, media managers, or internal business software often only need the rendering engine and a few web APIs. Features like the built-in PDF viewer, Wallet, Translate, Media Router, and similar browser functionality may never be used, yet they are still bundled with every application.

It would be nice if developers had a way to avoid shipping optional Chromium features that their application doesn't need.

### Proposed Solution

One possible approach would be to introduce a build configuration file, something similar to `electron.config.js`, where developers could enable or disable supported Chromium components before packaging.

For example:

```js
module.exports = {
  chromium: {
    pdfViewer: false,
    wallet: false,
    translate: false,
    mediaRouter: false,
    autofill: false
  }
};
```

If no configuration file is present, Electron would continue to behave exactly as it does today.

Only components that are considered optional and safe to exclude would be configurable. Anything required by Electron or Chromium would simply remain enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

I also thought about having separate Electron distributions, such as a "minimal" build and a "full" build.

However, I think a configuration-based approach would be more flexible. Different applications have different requirements, so allowing developers to choose which optional features they need seems more practical than maintaining multiple Electron distributions.

### Additional Information

I understand that Chromium has many internal dependencies and that not every feature can simply be removed.

The goal isn't to make every Chromium component optional, but to provide a supported way to exclude features that are already considered optional.

Even if only a small number of components could be configured this way, it could still help reduce application size and avoid shipping functionality that some applications will never use.

Building Electron takes hours even on modern machines and requires hundreds of gigabytes of storage space.

You can use https://github.com/electron/build-tools to make your own builds and various build flags to reduce the build size. (You'll need to dig through the code to find them though.)

I don't think it's realistic for the project to provide multiple distributions. It's difficult (and expensive) enough to make all of our current builds. I don't think we have the capacity to add more complexity there.

I'll leave the issue open though to see if other maintainers disagree. I definitely understand why the features would be useful. I just don't think they're feasible at the moment, unfortunately.

Thanks for the response!

I think I may not have explained the idea very well.

I wasn't suggesting another official build variation or asking Electron to maintain multiple distributions.

What I had in mind was a feature in the existing build system. For example, a specific config.js, the build could check that configuration and exclude supported optional Chromium features. If no configuration is provided, the build would behave exactly as it does today and include everything. Maybe there aren't any optional features. I don't know, but if there are, it could be useful for Electron.

It's just an idea because the Electron developers know the Chromium codebase much better than I do.

I will look at the build tools too. Thanks again.

You can find some build flags in the Electron and Chromium source code that can do that, e.g., one to disable the extension logic or one to disable the printing code. build-tools places config files on your computer where you can persist those variables. You'll need to recompile Electron though, which takes hours and requires hundreds of GB of disk space. I believe it's not really feasible to exclude features when an app is packaged.
Closing per @nikwen's comments, excluding features at package time isn't something we can realistically support.

nodes.title: [Bug]: globalShortcut.register() returns true before the Wayland portal bind resolves
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (also 42.5.1 with the portal path enabled via flags)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (GNOME Wayland, gnome-shell 50.1, xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.1)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

On the Linux Wayland portal path, an app can find out whether a `globalShortcut.register()` call actually resulted in a bound shortcut — or at minimum, `register()`/`isRegistered()` should not report success when the portal denied the bind.

### Actual Behavior

On Wayland, `globalShortcut` goes through the `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` portal (`GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux`). The portal's `BindShortcuts` call is asynchronous and consent-gated (GNOME shows a dialog before binding), so the synchronous boolean returned by `register()` cannot be truthful on this path: `GlobalShortcut::Register()` returns `true` as soon as the command set is handed to the listener via `OnCommandsChanged()`, before the bind resolves. `isRegistered()` is equally misleading — it only consults the local command map.

If the portal later replies with an error — e.g. GNOME 50.0/50.1 rejects `BindShortcuts` for any app id that fails `g_application_id_is_valid()` (see gnome-control-center `global-shortcuts-provider`; relaxed in 50.2), or the user dismisses the consent dialog — the result dies in `GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux::OnBindShortcuts()` as a `LOG(ERROR)`. Nothing reaches `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` observers, so Electron has no way to surface it even if it wanted to.

Observed on an Ubuntu 26.04 VM with stock Electron binaries (`GlobalShortcutsPortal` + `GlobalShortcutsPortalPreferredTrigger` enabled):

```
# invalid app id (dashed desktopName, no dot): register() lies, portal denies
20:32:28 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
dbus: error_name=org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed reply_serial=23
(shortcut never fires, no dialog shown)

# valid reverse-DNS desktopName (com.example.MyApp.desktop): works end to end
20:41:49 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
20:44:34 FIRED Control+Shift+F10        # after one consent dialog
20:46:38 REGISTER ... -> true            # relaunch: silent re-bind, persists
```

Apps cannot distinguish three genuinely different states: **bound**, **pending consent**, and **denied**. That matters in practice — "shortcut silently doesn't work" is indistinguishable from "user hasn't clicked the consent dialog yet".

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Surfacing the bind result needs a small Chromium patch: `OnBindShortcuts()` receives the response but `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` has no observer/callback for it today.

Proposed minimal API (shape open for discussion): keep `register()` synchronous — its boolean means "request submitted" on this path — and add a module event that fires when the portal resolves the bind:

```js
globalShortcut.on('registration-resolved', (accelerator, bound) => {
  // bound === false: portal denied (invalid app id, user dismissed dialog, ...)
})
```

Alternatives considered: a promise-returning `registerAsync()`, or a callback in an options object. On non-portal platforms the event could fire immediately with the `register()` result, keeping it usable cross-platform.

Draft PR with plumbing to follow; API shape needs API WG input.
@VerteDinde Assigned you given that you have a PR open already.

#52224 added a `registration-resolved` event on `globalShortcut` for exactly this (main / 46, not backported), so apps can tell a bound shortcut from a denied one on the portal path. closing this out.
